chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya and 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife, then another man marries her after him, and she bears children to the second husband. Is the child of the second husband permissible for marriage to the child of the first husband (from another woman)? He said, 'Yes.'

And I asked him about a man who freed his concubine, then another man marries her after him, and she bears children to the second husband. Is her child permissible for marriage to the child of the one who freed her? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.خَلَّفَ عَلَيْهَا: married her / succeeded to her in marriage

ai.seo_question: Does a second marriage and childbirth create a permanent prohibition of marriage (mahram) between the new children and the previous family members?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *mahramiyyah* (marital affinity) through subsequent marriage, specifically addressing the status of children from a second union relative to the first husband or the man who freed the concubine. It establishes that the bond of affinity is created by the marriage contract itself, meaning the children of the second husband are considered in-laws to the first husband's offspring, facilitating marriage between them if other conditions are met. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that affinity arises from the valid marriage, regardless of whether the woman was previously married or a freed concubine.
